title: Module Deep Dive
story: Your math library has grown from 3 functions to 30 - spread across geometry, algebra, and statistics. One flat file is chaos. You need organized compartments that hide internal details and expose a clean public face. Modules to the rescue.
why: Modules organize code into logical groups with controlled visibility - pub items are accessible externally, private items are hidden implementation details.
analogy: A restaurant kitchen has a public dining area (pub functions) where customers interact, and a private kitchen (private functions) where only chefs work. Customers don't need to know about the vegetable chopper or the stock pot - they just see the finished dishes.
try_it: Add more functions to the stats module: `median_of_three(a, b, c)` that returns the middle value, and `pub fn standard_deviation` that uses private helpers. Try calling a private function from main - observe the compiler error.
tips: Default is private - you must explicitly mark everything you want to expose
Use `pub` on items you're willing to maintain as a stable API
Private helpers can change freely without breaking code outside the module
common_mistakes: Marking everything pub by default - only expose what's necessary
Forgetting `use module_name;` before accessing module items
Trying to access private items from outside the module
